fixes: P1, light state and colour act missing. Storyboard Act V for S22-S24 calls for the two window panes plus the desk's candle pools (3200 K, key:fill 4:1, the surround sinking to near-black), a left candle on f1664, a right candle on 'age' f1707 that reveals the far side of the board, and a candle swell f1744-1760. What was delivered is flat, uniform light: at f1664 the 8x5 luma grid varies by under 2% (178-182/255). The coded 'key pool' cannot be seen. Nothing happens on f1707, and the +0.25 EV swell is a global exposure ramp. The desk chrome is out of scope, but its light on the board is not. Render the left pool from f1664 and add the right pool on f1707 (R25 point lights in 2D; Eevee point/area lights from f1725). Darken the frame edges, swell the pools themselves (not global exposure) into f1760, and start converging toward the game's daylight only after that. Without this the 2D phase reads as a strategy-map reveal, not a tapestry waking by candlelight.

P1, material pop at the moment of peel-up breaks the central metaphor. Example: Grandbois f1727 is a stitched elevation; at f1728 it is replaced in one frame by a clean, unstitched game-model render lying flat, which then hinges up. Every town and site does the same. The storyboard's pop-up rule (S21, carried into S23-S24) is that the front faces keep exactly the stitch texture they had when flat. Project the R25 radiance and normals of the stitched icon onto the model's front faces for the hinge, and cross-dissolve to the stitch-port material only after the piece is upright (about 6-8 frames), so the cloth itself is seen to become the piece.

P1, glitch on the hero town during the crane: at f1736-1737 Grandbois loses its floor. Green satin shows through inside the walls and the houses read as floating roofs, then the floor pops back at f1738 (confirmed in decoded mp4 frame n=72). It is probably the coupon swell or padding-press mask rising above the town base on that pose. Clamp the board height under every town footprint for every frame of the rise, not only the settled pose, and recheck every town over f1728-1760 at 1:1.

P2, the climax lands on stillness. Pitch is 76.3 at f1740 and 67.3 at f1750, so the crane is 95% done by f1750. Optical flow peaks at 4.5 px/frame over f1736-1744 and falls below 0.4 by f1755. The last piece starts at f1748. The music's loudest passage (f1744-1783, bass swell f1755, peak f1760) therefore plays over a board that is almost still for about 30 frames, and with the valance out of scope nothing lands on f1755 or f1760. Shift the crane's velocity peak to about f1742-1746 with a long ease-out that genuinely lands at f1760-1766, as the storyboard states. Schedule the hero beats onto the music: the outer towns (Sablon, Hautecouronne) and Grandbois's banner should finish on f1755-1760. Make the swell a visible candle-pool brightening.

P2, the end state does not yet read as the menu board. The registration is excellent: hex grid, coast, Grandbois, Hautecouronne, the sea's gold claim borders, and a sea colour of #2F5C83 against the menu's #275A81. But permanent dark castle-shaped footprints remain on the crop and forest hexes north of every town at f1782, which the menu does not have. The wheat is much lighter (OKLab L 0.69 against 0.51 on the top wheat hexes; L 0.54 against 0.48 over the whole right half), the pines are sparse and pale, and the towns are low. The storyboard's S24 step is not implemented: from f1756 the board albedo should blend into a projection of the 2x UI-free menu plate, masked where pieces are still settling. Implement it. Also heal footprints, with the padding and satin closing back, once their 12 frames or more have been shown.

P2, story continuity with S20-S22. The storyboard has the S20 banner and the S21 village already standing at Grandbois through f1664-1719 (the banner's sway decaying to rest by f1719), with the village growing settle_1 -> settle_2 into Grandbois. The PoC opens on bare linen with nothing standing, and Grandbois peels up as a fresh icon. As a result the wavefront's origin is unmotivated, and the PoC would not cut against f1663. Even in the narrowed scope, place the risen village and banner (EV-DM/P layer) on Grandbois from f1664, so the world visibly grows out of the first home.

P3, the wavefront reads as hex tiles. Each ring of hexes appears on the same frame as flat, sharp-edged colour pads; at f1672 six hexes appear at once, and only then does strand 'confetti' sweep across them. Stagger the starts within a ring (azimuth plus noise, about ±3-5 frames). Bring the padding colour in under the advancing strand front instead of as a whole-hex pad. Let the sea flood continuously across hex seams rather than in discrete hex pads. Also, the first visible stitch is at f1666; put it on the f1664 bass frame.

P3, the elevation icons straddle the neighbouring hexes. The Grandbois castle is stitched across the two hexes north of Grandbois, so in the face-on board f1690-1725 the towns appear to sit on the wrong hexes, which weakens recognition of the game layout. Shorten or foreshorten the elevations so each stays inside its own hex, or use plan-plus-elevation icons as the brief asks.

P3, the tether-snap beat does not read at full frame. At 1:1 the tethers look like straight pale rods, as at Hautecouronne f1739. Thicken them, give them a wool colour and a sag, and add a visible recoil, so the release is legible on the pieces the eye follows (the five towns).
praise: The timing structure is right, and I checked each point against the encoded mp4. The audio slice is sample-exact: 0-sample offset, correlation 0.9986, 119 frames. The wavefront grows from Grandbois, its last change lands on f1718, and the board holds from f1719 to f1725. The R25-to-Eevee swap cannot be seen: the blurred mean difference stays at 0.7/255 or less, about the level of the grain. The crane starts on the f1726 'remembered' bass, moves on ones without stray motion, and lands on the decoded menu pose. At f1782 the board registers with the live menu almost perfectly: hex grid, coastline, Grandbois and Hautecouronne positions, the sea's gold realm-claim borders, and a sea colour within a few dE of the game's. Pieces rise in a stagger outward from Grandbois on twos, keep their footprints open, and are all settled by f1760. The face-on embroidered board at f1726 is a convincing piece of craft and reads clearly as 'the game, made of thread'.
